messages.text:
Noor is excited about the methods desk and the chance to build it with Finch. The nine-month editorial project is the only fixed constraint on capacity — it ends in March. Until then, Noor can commit three days a week. Starting in April, that moves to four days.

The outside project is separate: it has its own funding, data, and publication pipeline. Nothing from it — data, drafts, or intellectual property — will transfer to Finch. It runs in parallel and stays independent. We'll want a clean conflict wall in the agreement.

On authority: Noor needs final say on methods corrections. That's non-negotiable for the desk's credibility.

Compensation: $125k annualized at 1.0 FTE. At three days (0.6 FTE) that's $75k; at four days (0.8 FTE) it's $100k. We can structure it as a prorated salary with a step-up in April, or a retainer plus project fees — open on mechanics.

Title is flexible. A six-month review milestone (around the March transition) makes sense to recalibrate scope, resources, and whether the desk should scale further.

What does Finch need to see in a first draft?

Finch proposes a salaried appointment as Methods Editor at **$125,000 annualized at 1.0 FTE**, with responsibility for training a deputy. Noor would work three days a week through March at a $75,000 annual salary rate, then move to four days in April at a $100,000 annual salary rate.

**Desk coverage.** By December, the desk needs to accept and triage submissions on four fixed weekdays. Finch would assign a deputy to cover the fourth day through March. During Noor’s three scheduled days, Noor would train the deputy and document how to log submissions, flag urgent issues, and hand off cases. The deputy could acknowledge submissions and request missing materials. Urgent cases on the deputy’s day would go to the editor-in-chief, who could pause a story pending Noor’s review. This keeps Noor’s fourth day free through March.

**Disputed corrections.** Noor would have final say on the desk’s technical finding, including whether a methods error occurred and whether proposed wording fixes it. The editor-in-chief would retain final authority over what Finch publishes. If they disagree, Noor would record the finding and proposed correction, and the editor-in-chief would record the publication decision and reasons. Finch would publish a short editor’s note disclosing any unresolved technical objection if it keeps the disputed passage online. Only wording Noor approves could carry the desk’s endorsement. Would that give Noor the authority needed to stand behind the desk’s work?

**Outside project.** Each project would retain its own funding, files, data, drafts, and intellectual property. Noor would flag overlapping submissions to the editor-in-chief and recuse from their assignment, review, and correction. The editor-in-chief would appoint an independent reviewer for those cases.

We propose holding the review in March so both sides can use the intake volume, turnaround times, and deputy workload to plan April staffing. The four-day schedule and salary increase would take effect in April regardless of that review. If the corrections provision works for Noor, the remaining scheduling question is which three weekdays Noor can commit to through March so Finch can assign the deputy’s day.

The framework works. The corrections provision gives Noor the technical authority the desk needs — final say on the finding and the fix, with a transparent record when the editor-in-chief overrules on publication. The editor's note mechanism protects the desk's credibility. The conflict wall is clean: separate IP, mandatory recusal, independent reviewer.

Three questions before we lock in the weekdays:

1. **Conflict scope.** "Overlapping submissions" — does that cover only manuscripts that physically overlap with the outside project's manuscripts, or also submissions in the same narrow methodological domain where Noor's outside-project expertise could create a perceived conflict? Noor would prefer the broader reading (domain-level) to avoid any appearance issue.

2. **Deputy hiring timeline.** You need the deputy trained and covering a fixed day by December. When does Finch plan to post/hire? Noor's training capacity on three days is real but not infinite — if hiring slips, the December coverage target slips.

3. **March review outputs.** The review informs April staffing, but the four-day step-up is automatic. What else should the review cover? Noor would want to look at: intake volume vs. capacity, deputy workload sustainability, whether the desk needs a second deputy or a different coverage model at four days, and any corrections-process friction that emerged.

On weekdays: Noor can commit **Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday** through March. That leaves Monday and Friday for the outside project's fixed commitments and gives Finch a contiguous three-day block for desk operations. Deputy takes Monday or Friday — Finch's call.

If the conflict scope and hiring timeline are workable, we can move to drafting.

Finch proposes **Monday through Thursday for submissions**, with the deputy covering Monday and Noor working Tuesday through Thursday through March. Noor would add Monday in April. That gives Noor and the deputy a Tuesday handoff and keeps urgent Monday decisions with the editor-in-chief.

**Conflict scope.** Finch accepts domain-level recusal. Before intake opens, Noor and the editor-in-chief would describe the outside project’s narrow methodological domain in writing, without sharing project materials. A submission within that domain would go directly to an independent reviewer, even when it involves different authors, data, and manuscripts. The editor-in-chief would resolve borderline cases before Noor sees the materials. For recused cases, the independent reviewer would hold the desk’s authority over the technical finding and proposed fix.

**Deputy timeline.** Finch proposes to designate an existing editor as interim deputy by November 30 and post the permanent role that day, with a target appointment by December 18. Four-day intake would open the week of December 1, with December 7 as the first deputy Monday. Finch would prepare the written intake and escalation procedure before launch and reserve two 90-minute blocks within Noor’s December 1–3 schedule for training and a practice handoff. The interim deputy would log submissions, request missing materials, and escalate urgent cases to the editor-in-chief. If the permanent hire takes longer, the interim deputy would continue Monday coverage. Noor would train the permanent deputy during scheduled desk hours.

**March review.** Finch agrees to all four topics. The review would produce a written April staffing decision covering intake volume against capacity, deputy workload, and whether to retain Monday support, add a second deputy, or redistribute coverage. Noor and the editor-in-chief would also review disputed corrections and recusals, record any agreed procedural changes, and assign responsibility and dates for implementing them. Noor’s move to four days and the $100,000 annual salary rate would take effect April 1 regardless of the review outcome.

Finch is ready to draft on those terms.

Terms are solid. Three confirmations before drafting:

1. **Interim deputy bandwidth.** An existing editor taking Monday coverage plus their current duties through at least December 18 — does Finch have capacity confirmation from that editor and their manager? Noor's December training blocks (Dec 2–3) assume the interim deputy is present and not pulled elsewhere.

2. **Domain description deadline.** The written domain description needs to be finished before intake opens December 1. Who drafts it, and by what date? Noor can provide the domain parameters by November 15; editor-in-chief finalizes by November 22.

3. **Independent reviewer pool.** For recused cases, the independent reviewer holds full desk authority (finding + fix). Finch should identify at least two qualified reviewers before launch so coverage isn't dependent on one person's availability.

If those are in hand, Noor is ready to sign. Send the draft.

**Draft appointment agreement**

1. **Appointment and pay.** Finch Review appoints Noor as Methods Editor effective December 1, 2026, with responsibility for establishing the methods desk and training its deputy. The full-time annual salary rate is $125,000. Noor will work Tuesday through Thursday at 0.6 FTE, paid at a $75,000 annual rate, through March 31, 2027. On April 1, Noor will add Monday and move to 0.8 FTE at a $100,000 annual rate. The increase is automatic.

2. **Intake and deputy coverage.** The desk will open for submissions December 1 and take submissions Monday through Thursday, with December 7 as the first deputy Monday. Finch has yet to obtain written capacity confirmations from the interim deputy and their manager. By November 30, Finch will provide Noor with a named deputy’s acceptance and their manager’s written commitment to protect Monday coverage and two 90-minute training blocks, one each on December 2 and 3. The manager will identify who covers competing duties during those hours. If the first editor is unavailable, Finch will secure another editor on the same terms by November 30. The assignment will run until the permanent deputy has completed training and can take over. Finch will post the role by November 30 and target December 18 for appointment.

3. **Review procedure.** Finch will prepare a written intake procedure before launch. On Mondays, the deputy will screen for conflicts, log submissions, request missing materials, escalate urgent cases to the editor-in-chief, and prepare a Tuesday handoff for Noor. The editor-in-chief may pause a story pending technical review. Noor will review the procedure with the deputy and supervise a practice handoff during the December training blocks. All deputy training will take place within Noor’s scheduled days.

4. **Outside project and recusal.** Noor may continue to direct the outside project. Each project will retain its own funding, data, drafts, publication process, and intellectual property. Because November 15 and 22 have passed, Finch proposes November 27 for Noor to provide a short description of the narrow methodological domain and November 30 for the editor-in-chief to finalize the screening criteria with Noor. The description need only identify the domain. Finch will route submissions in that domain to an independent reviewer before Noor sees the materials, including submissions with different authors or data. The editor-in-chief will resolve borderline cases. Noor will recuse from assignment, review, and correction of covered submissions.

5. **Independent reviewers.** By November 30, Finch will give Noor the names and qualifications of at least two reviewers with relevant methods expertise who have confirmed availability and independence from the outside project. Finch will check for case-specific conflicts before assignment. In a recused case, the assigned reviewer holds the desk’s full authority over the technical finding and whether a proposed correction resolves it.

6. **Disputed corrections.** Noor has final say on the desk’s technical finding and the adequacy of a fix, with the assigned independent reviewer exercising that authority in recused cases. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority. If a disagreement persists, the technical reviewer will record the finding and proposed fix, and the editor-in-chief will record the publication decision and reasons. If Finch publishes or keeps a disputed passage online, it will attach an editor’s note disclosing the unresolved technical objection. Desk endorsement requires the technical reviewer’s approval of the published wording.

7. **March review.** Noor and the editor-in-chief will compare intake volume with capacity, assess deputy workload, and review how corrections and recusals have worked. Finch will record its April staffing decision, including whether to retain Monday support, add a second deputy, or redistribute coverage. The review will identify who is responsible for each agreed procedural change and when it will take effect.

Finch will send this draft for signature once it can attach the deputy and manager confirmations, the agreed domain description, and the two reviewer confirmations.

Accepted. The draft matches every term we agreed.

Noor will provide the domain description by **November 27**. Finch will attach the three confirmations — interim deputy + manager, finalized domain criteria, two independent reviewers — and send the final agreement for signature.

We're good to proceed.
